title: React Fundamentals
description: Core concepts: state, hooks, props, and rendering.

cards.front: Why must React state updates be immutable?
cards.back: React compares object references to detect changes and decide when to re-render components.

cards.front: When should you prefer useReducer over useState?
cards.back: When state logic involves multiple sub-values or complex transitions where the next state depends on the previous one.

cards.front: What does the <Outlet /> component do in React Router?
cards.back: It acts as a placeholder inside a parent route layout where matching child routes are rendered.

cards.front: What is a controlled form input in React?
cards.back: An input whose value is driven by React state and updated through an onChange event handler.

title: Web Accessibility (a11y)
description: Essential practices for keyboard navigation, semantics, and ARIA.

cards.front: Why should icon-only buttons include an aria-label?
cards.back: Because there is no visible text for screen readers to announce the button's purpose.

cards.front: Why use semantic HTML elements like <main>, <nav>, and <button>?
cards.back: They provide built-in keyboard behavior and landmark navigation for assistive technologies.

cards.front: What is the purpose of proper heading hierarchy (h1 to h3)?
cards.back: It creates a clear document outline that helps screen reader users jump directly between sections.
